mainTopic: Is תפילין time-bound (proven through women's obligation)? Plus found תכלת, and whether people go to the trouble of imitating מצוה objects
overview: The amud continues the search for a תנא who holds that תפילין is not time-bound, which would mean women are obligated and שבת is a time for תפילין. First the גמרא rejects the proof from מיכל בת כושי: maybe that תנא follows רבי יוסי, who lets women do מצוות voluntarily, as the story of יונה's wife going up for the רגל shows. The גמרא then brings the ברייתא of someone who finds תפילין. There both רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה let a woman bring them in. When the גמרא asks whether that too might be only optional, it proves that neither רבי מאיר (from a סתם משנה about שופר) nor רבי יהודה (from a סתם ספרא about סמיכה) holds like רבי יוסי. A new topic follows: רבי אלעזר rules that found תכלת strips are unfit, but threads are fit. After several challenges, the threads are narrowed to twisted ones cut to length, because people do not go to that much trouble. רבא challenges this using the משנה that worries new תפילין may be amulets, and he concludes that whether people go to such trouble is a dispute between תנאים. He begins quoting a ברייתא to show this dispute, and the quote continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Maybe the case of מיכל follows רבי יוסי: women may choose to do it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from מיכל בת כושי by saying it may follow רבי יוסי, who holds that women may optionally do סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows רבי יוסי, who said: women may lay hands on a קרבן if they wish (it is optional).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is pushing back on the proof it just brought. The חכמים did not stop מיכל from wearing תפילין, but that may be only because women are allowed to do such מצוות voluntarily.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier proof assumed that if women may wear תפילין, they must be obligated, which would make תפילין not time-bound. רבי יוסי shows another possibility: women may do a מצוה even without being obligated. So the silence of the חכמים proves nothing about whether תפילין is time-bound.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaning one's hands on the head of a קרבן before it is slaughtered
Optional: allowed but not required

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי is not saying women are obligated in סמיכה. He is saying they are permitted to do it if they want. That difference is the whole point here.

phrases.english: It follows Rabbi Yosei, who said:
phrases.notes: This picks up from before: maybe the תנא who told the מיכל story agrees with רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: Women may lay hands on a sacrifice, optionally.
phrases.notes: Women are not obligated, but they may perform it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי, דְּאָמַר: נָשִׁים סוֹמְכוֹת רְשׁוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from מיכל בת כושי (stated on the previous amud) by offering another way to read the case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that the תנא of the מיכל story holds תפילין is not time-bound.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that permission for women means obligation for women. Under רבי יוסי, women may voluntarily do מצוות they are not obligated in.

steps.title: Support for the rejection: יונה's wife went up for the festival
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that this תנא must hold women act voluntarily, because he also lets יונה's wife go up for the רגל, which everyone agrees is time-bound.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you do not say so: the wife of יונה used to go up for the festival pilgrimage, and they did not protest. Is there anyone who says the festival pilgrimage is not a time-bound positive מצוה? Rather, he must hold it was optional for her. Here too, with תפילין, it is optional.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the rejection from step 1. The same ברייתא says nobody stopped יונה's wife from going to ירושלים for the רגל, even though women are clearly not obligated in that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that עלייה לרגל is a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא, so women are exempt. Since the חכמים still did not protest, this תנא must allow women to do מצוות voluntarily (רשות). That same reasoning explains מיכל and תפילין, so the earlier proof is fully removed.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you do not say so: introduces a proof that you must accept the idea just stated
Going up to ירושלים for the pilgrimage festival
Protested or objected
A positive מצוה tied to a specific time; women are exempt
Here too: applies the same logic to the current case

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that "the חכמים did not protest" is weak evidence for obligation. It may only show permission.

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
phrases.notes: Meaning: if you do not say this תנא agrees with רבי יוסי.

phrases.aramaic: אִשְׁתּוֹ שֶׁל יוֹנָה הָיְתָה עוֹלָה לָרֶגֶל
phrases.english: the wife of Yonah would go up for the festival pilgrimage
phrases.notes: From the same ברייתא as the מיכל story.

phrases.english: and they did not protest against her.
phrases.notes: The Sages did not stop her.

phrases.english: Is there anyone who says
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question: of course nobody says this.

phrases.english: that the festival pilgrimage is not a positive commandment
that is caused by time?
phrases.notes: It happens only on the festivals, so it is clearly time-bound.

phrases.english: Rather, he holds it is optional,
phrases.notes: The תנא held she went voluntarily.

phrases.english: here too, it is optional.
phrases.notes: So מיכל also wore תפילין voluntarily. No proof can be drawn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves that the רבי יוסי reading from step 1 is the correct way to understand the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That the תנא of the מיכל ברייתא holds women may do non-obligatory מצוות as רשות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The same ברייתא's case of יונה's wife going up for the רגל, which is undisputedly time-bound.

steps.title: A new source: the ברייתא about finding תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a different ברייתא as the source for a תנא who holds תפילין is not time-bound: a man or woman who finds תפילין brings them in pair by pair.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is this תנא, as it was taught: One who finds תפילין brings them in pair by pair, whether a man or a woman, whether new or old. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה forbids this for new ones and permits it for old ones.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the מיכל proof, the גמרא finds another ברייתא to answer the question of which תנא holds that שבת is a time for תפילין. Here it quotes that ברייתא; the next step draws the lesson from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is someone who finds תפילין lying exposed on שבת. They may save them by wearing them in, one pair at a time, because worn תפילין count as clothing, not carrying. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue only about new תפילין, which might just be amulets, versus old ones, which are surely real תפילין.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, it is this תנא: introduces a replacement source
One who finds תפילין (here, on שבת out in the open)
Pair by pair: wearing one set at a time
New / old תפילין

phrases.english: Rather, it is this tanna
phrases.notes: Who holds that שבת is a time for תפילין? This one.

phrases.english: as it was taught:
phrases.notes: This quotes a ברייתא from the תוספתא.

phrases.english: One who finds tefillin brings them in pair by pair.
phrases.notes: He wears each pair inside, which counts as wearing, not carrying.

phrases.english: Whether a man or a woman,
phrases.notes: A woman may also do this.

phrases.english: whether new ones or old ones,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda forbids it with new ones,
phrases.notes: New ones may be amulets rather than real תפילין, so they are not clothing.

phrases.english: and permits it with old ones.
phrases.notes: Old ones are surely real תפילין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the מיכל proof was rejected, the גמרא replaces it with a new source.
steps.raayaObject: That some תנא holds תפילין is a מצוה not bound by time, so שבת is a time for תפילין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of הַמּוֹצֵא תְּפִילִּין (רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה).

steps.title: Both תנאים agree about a woman, so תפילין is not time-bound
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue only about new versus old תפילין and not about a woman, both hold that women are obligated, which means תפילין is a מצוה not bound by time.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue only about new and old ones, but about a woman they do not argue. Learn from this that תפילין is a positive מצוה not caused by time, and women are obligated in every positive מצוה not caused by time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the lesson from the ברייתא in step 3. Neither תנא objects to a woman bringing in the תפילין, so both must hold that women are obligated in תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים let a woman wear the found תפילין in on שבת. The גמרא reads that as showing she is obligated in תפילין. Women are obligated only in מצוות not bound by time, so this תנא holds תפילין applies at all times, including שבת. The next step will ask whether 'optional' could explain this too, as it did for מיכל.

keyTerms.meaning: They argue only up to this point: limits the dispute to one issue
Learn from it: draws the conclusion
A positive מצוה not tied to time; women are obligated
Obligated (feminine plural)

steps.whatToRemember: The מיכל story was rejected as proof because women may act voluntarily (רבי יוסי). The ברייתא of הַמּוֹצֵא תְּפִילִּין, where both רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה let a woman bring in the תפילין, shows a תנא who holds תפילין is not time-bound, so women are obligated and שבת is a time for תפילין.
steps.whyThisMatters: This identifies the תנא who holds שבת is a time for תפילין, which is the question the sugya has been searching for.

phrases.english: They disagree only
about new ones and old ones,
but about a woman they do not disagree.
phrases.notes: Both allow a woman to bring them in.

phrases.english: Learn from it

phrases.aramaic: מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁלֹּא הַזְּמַן גְּרָמָא הוּא,
phrases.english: that it is a positive commandment not caused by time,
phrases.notes: תפילין applies even on שבת and at night, according to this תנא.

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁאֵין הַזְּמַן גְּרָמָא
phrases.english: and every positive commandment not caused by time,
women are obligated.
phrases.notes: So a woman may wear them in, as the ברייתא says.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי אֶלָּא בַּחֲדָשׁוֹת וִישָׁנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the ברייתא quoted in step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The תנא of הַמּוֹצֵא תְּפִילִּין holds תפילין is a מצות עשה שלא הזמן גרמא. Women are therefore obligated, and שבת is a time for תפילין according to him.

steps.title: Maybe this תנא lets women do it only as an option
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the conclusion. Maybe the תנא who lets a woman bring in תפילין holds like רבי יוסי, who says women may optionally do time-bound מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe he holds like רבי יוסי, who said that women may optionally do סמיכה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the conclusion it just reached. Maybe women handle תפילין only because they are allowed to, not because they are obligated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof that תפילין is not time-bound depended on women being obligated. But if this תנא follows רבי יוסי, then women may do even time-bound מצוות voluntarily. In that case, a woman bringing in תפילין proves nothing about whether תפילין is time-bound.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps (introduces a possible alternative explanation)
They (women) lean their hands on a קרבן before it is slaughtered (סמיכה)
Optional: allowed, but not required

steps.confusionAlert: This looks just like the challenge in step 1, but it is aimed at a different target. Step 1 was about the proof from מיכל בת כושי. Here the challenge is against the new ברייתא about finding תפילין, which is the source the גמרא now relies on.

phrases.english: But perhaps he holds like Rabbi Yosei,
who said: women may lean their hands on an offering as an option?
phrases.notes: The reasoning would then be: just as women may optionally do סמיכה, they may optionally handle תפילין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 4 by offering another reason why women could handle תפילין.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that women are obligated in תפילין, and therefore that תפילין is not time-bound
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If women may optionally do time-bound מצוות (like רבי יוסי holds), then a woman handling תפילין does not show that she is obligated.

steps.title: Neither רבי מאיר nor רבי יהודה holds like רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the challenge. Neither רבי מאיר nor רבי יהודה agrees with רבי יוסי's view that women may do time-bound מצוות optionally.
steps.simpleTranslation: That cannot be. רבי מאיר does not hold like רבי יוסי, and רבי יהודה does not hold like רבי יוסי either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in one sentence. It is also setting up the next two steps, which will prove this claim for each תנא separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא about finding תפילין is a dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה. If neither of them accepts the idea of optional time-bound מצוות for women, then the challenge has nothing to stand on. So whatever women do here must come from being obligated.

keyTerms.meaning: This cannot enter your mind; that idea is impossible

phrases.english: This cannot enter your mind

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: because Rabbi Meir does not hold like Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda does not hold like Rabbi Yosei

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denies the premise: the תנאים involved do not hold of optional time-bound מצוות for women
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא might follow רבי יוסי, so women's handling of תפילין would only be optional.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה reject רבי יוסי's view, so women's involvement must come from obligation.

steps.title: Proof for רבי מאיר from the שופר משנה
steps.stepSummary: An unattributed משנה says we do not stop children from blowing שופר. That implies we do stop women. Since unattributed משניות follow רבי מאיר, he does not allow women to do time-bound מצוות optionally.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר does not hold like רבי יוסי, as we learned in a משנה: we do not stop children from blowing שופר. This implies that we do stop women. And an unattributed משנה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the first half of its answer: רבי מאיר disagrees with רבי יוסי. It uses an inference from a משנה about שופר on ראש השנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says only that children may not be stopped. That implies women, who are exempt from this time-bound מצוה, must be stopped. If women could do time-bound מצוות optionally, there would be no reason to stop them. Since a סתם משנה is רבי מאיר, this shows רבי מאיר's view.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold back / stop someone from doing something
Young children
This implies; it introduces an inference from what the text left out
An unattributed משנה, which follows רבי מאיר

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה never mentions women directly. The point about women comes from an inference (הָא): since only children were allowed, women must not be.

phrases.aramaic: לָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir does not hold like Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: אֵין מְעַכְּבִין אֶת הַתִּינוֹקוֹת מִלִּתְקוֹעַ.
phrases.english: as we learned: we do not stop the children from blowing the shofar.
phrases.notes: Children are allowed so they can practice for when they will be obligated.

phrases.english: This implies that women we do stop —
and an unattributed Mishnah is Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the first half of step 6's answer.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר does not allow women to do time-bound מצוות optionally
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in ראש השנה: אין מעכבין את התינוקות מלתקוע, together with the rule that a סתם משנה follows רבי מאיר

steps.title: Proof for רבי יהודה from the ספרא on סמיכה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא in the ספרא learns from the פסוק that only men do סמיכה and women do not. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון disagree and say women may do it optionally.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה does not hold like רבי יוסי either, as a ברייתא teaches: "Speak to the sons of Israel... and he shall lean." The sons of Israel lean their hands, but the daughters of Israel do not. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say: women may lean their hands as an option.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins proving the second half of its answer: רבי יהודה disagrees with רבי יוסי. It quotes a ברייתא where the unnamed first opinion says women do not do סמיכה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The unnamed first opinion reads the word "sons" as leaving out women entirely, not even as an option. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון are named separately as disagreeing. So the unnamed view clearly rejects the optional approach. The next line will identify who that unnamed view is.

keyTerms.meaning: The sons of Israel (men)
The daughters of Israel (women)

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda does not hold like Rabbi Yosei,
as it was taught: "Speak to the sons of Israel... and he shall lean",
phrases.notes: These words come from ויקרא א:ב–ד.

phrases.english: the sons of Israel lean their hands
but the daughters of Israel do not lean their hands.
Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon say:
women may lean their hands as an option.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second half of step 6's answer.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה does not allow women to do time-bound מצוות optionally
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in the ספרא on ויקרא about סמיכה

steps.title: The unnamed ספרא is רבי יהודה, so the proof is complete
steps.stepSummary: An unattributed ספרא follows רבי יהודה. So רבי יהודה is the one who says women may not do סמיכה at all, and he rejects רבי יוסי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who is the author of an unattributed ספרא? רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the author of the unnamed opinion in the ספרא as רבי יהודה. This finishes the proof and closes the whole challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה are shown to reject optional time-bound מצוות for women. So when they let a woman bring in תפילין, it must be because she is obligated. That brings back the conclusion: תפילין is a מצוה not bound by time.

keyTerms.meaning: An unattributed teaching in the ספרא (the halachic מדרש on ויקרא), which follows רבי יהודה
Who is it? (asks who the author is)

steps.whatToRemember: Neither רבי מאיר (from the סתם משנה about שופר) nor רבי יהודה (from the סתם ספרא about סמיכה) holds like רבי יוסי. So in the ברייתא about finding תפילין, women are treated as obligated, which shows that תפילין is not a time-bound מצוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common tool of the גמרא: unnamed sources are identified with specific תנאים (סתם משנה is רבי מאיר, סתם ספרא is רבי יהודה). The גמרא then uses that to figure out what each תנא holds on other topics.

phrases.english: And an unattributed Sifra, whose is it? Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes step 8's proof by identifying the unnamed opinion as רבי יהודה, closing the challenge of step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה hold that women cannot optionally do time-bound מצוות. So their ruling about women and תפילין reflects an obligation, and תפילין is not time-bound.

steps.title: Found sky-blue wool: strips are unfit, threads are fit
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that תכלת strips found in the market are פסול for ציצית, while תכלת threads are כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: If someone finds תכלת in the marketplace, strips are unfit and threads are fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רבי אלעזר about blue wool found in the market and whether it can be used for ציצית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תכלת for ציצית must be made for the sake of the מצוה. Loose dyed strips could easily have been made for something else, so they are פסול. Threads are assumed to have been made for ציצית, so they are כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Sky-blue dyed wool used for one thread of ציצית
Strips (tufts) of combed, dyed wool that are not yet spun
Spun threads
Unfit / fit for use

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying the strips are not real תכלת. They may be genuine blue dye. The problem is only that we cannot assume they were made for the sake of ציצית.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
One who finds sky-blue wool in the marketplace:
if they are strips, they are unfit;
if they are threads, they are fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a new teaching. Like the found-תפילין case, it deals with whether we may assume a found object was made for a מצוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Found תכלת strips are פסול; found תכלת threads are כשר.

steps.title: Why not worry the threads were spun for a cloak too?
steps.stepSummary: If strips are suspected of being dyed for a cloak, the threads should also be suspected of being spun for a cloak.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about strips? We say they were dyed with a cloak in mind. Then for threads too, let us say they were spun with a cloak in mind!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר's distinction. It asks why the same worry does not apply to threads.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason strips are פסול is that they may have been dyed for weaving a garment. But weavers also spin thread for garments. So the threads should be suspect as well.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? (a challenge to a distinction)
With the intention of
A cloak or garment
He spun them

phrases.english: What is different about strips,
that we say: he dyed them with a cloak in mind?
Threads too, let us say:
he spun them with a cloak in mind!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the distinction made in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's ruling that threads are כשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The suspicion that disqualifies strips (made for a garment) applies equally to threads.

steps.title: The case is twisted threads
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר is speaking about twisted threads, which are not used for weaving.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is speaking about twisted threads.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing the case. The threads that are כשר are twisted ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Twisted, plied threads are not normally used to weave a cloak. So the worry that they were spun for a garment falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Twisted (plied) threads, the way ציצית strings are made

phrases.english: With twisted threads.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any threads, which could have been spun for a cloak
steps.terutzMaskana: Only twisted threads, which are not used for weaving

steps.title: Maybe twisted threads were made for a cloak's hem
steps.stepSummary: Even twisted threads might have been made to decorate the edge of a cloak.
steps.simpleTranslation: Twisted threads too, let us say he twisted them with the hem of a cloak in mind!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. Twisted threads are used for decorative fringes on garments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Twisted threads are not used for weaving, but they are used for ornamental edging. So the suspicion of a non-מצוה purpose comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: The edge or hem of a garment
He twisted (doubled) them

phrases.english: Twisted ones too, let us say:
he twisted them with the hem of a cloak in mind!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that twisted threads must have been made for ציצית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Twisted threads have another common use, as decorative fringe on a cloak's edge.

steps.title: Twisted threads already cut to fringe length
steps.stepSummary: The case is twisted threads cut into short pieces. People do not go to that much trouble for decoration.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is speaking about threads that were cut, since people certainly do not go to all this trouble.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the case even more, to twisted threads already cut into ציצית-sized pieces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Decorative edging is not cut into separate short strings shaped like ציצית. Nobody would bother to do that unless the threads were meant for ציצית. So we can assume they were made for the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Cut into separate lengths
People do not go to the trouble

steps.whyThisMatters: The principle 'people do not go to that much trouble' is the exact point רבא is about to challenge.

phrases.english: With ones that were cut,
for all this, certainly
people do not go to the trouble.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמוּפְסָקִין, דְּכוּלֵּי הַאי וַדַּאי לָא טָרְחִי אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Further narrowing of the case, supported by logic about human behavior
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any twisted threads, which could be decorative edging
steps.terutzMaskana: Twisted threads cut into separate lengths, which nobody makes except for ציצית

steps.title: רבא: people do go to such trouble, like amulets shaped as תפילין
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges the idea that people would not bother to imitate a מצוה object.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Does a person really go to the trouble of making an amulet that looks like תפילין?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges the reasoning from step 14 that people do not go to so much trouble.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's question sounds like 'nobody would do that.' Yet, as he will show, the משנה does worry that someone made an amulet shaped like תפילין. So we cannot rely on 'people don't bother.'

keyTerms.meaning: And does...? (a rhetorical question)
Goes to the trouble
An amulet

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying people do not make such amulets. His point is that even though it seems unlikely, the משנה still worries about it. So 'people don't bother' is not a reliable argument.

phrases.english: Rava said:
And does a person go to the trouble
to make an amulet in the form of תפילין?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning used in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle 'דכולי האי לא טרחי אינשי'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Making an amulet shaped like תפילין also seems like too much trouble, yet the משנה worries about it. So we should also worry about fringes made to look like ציצית.

steps.title: The משנה: only old תפילין must be brought in, not new ones
steps.stepSummary: The משנה about found תפילין applies only to old ones. New ones are exempt because they might be amulets.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: When is this said? With old ones. But with new ones, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings the משנה about finding תפילין on שבת to prove his challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Old, worn תפילין have clearly been used as תפילין, so one must rescue them. New ones might really be amulets made to look like תפילין, so there is no obligation. This shows the משנה does worry that people imitate מצוה objects.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case is this said? (limits a ruling)
Old (used) / new
Exempt

steps.whatToRemember: רבא uses the found-תפילין משנה to argue that we do worry people will imitate מצוה objects. This puts רבי אלעזר's reasoning about cut ציצית threads under pressure.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
In what case is this said? With old ones.
But with new ones, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind רבא's challenge in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That we do worry people take the trouble to imitate a מצוה object
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about found תפילין: old ones must be brought in, new ones are exempt

steps.title: רבי זירא's teaching about found תכלת supports the idea that people do not bother
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא tells his son אהבה to teach a ברייתא: strips of תכלת found in the market are unfit, but cut threads are fit, because a person does not go to that much trouble.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to his son אהבה: Go out and teach them this: If someone finds תכלת in the marketplace and it is in strips, it is unfit. If it is in cut threads, it is fit, because a person does not go to that much trouble.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא, taught by רבי זירא, that supports the earlier claim that people do not bother to imitate a מצוה object.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Strips of dyed wool may have been dyed with a cloak in mind, not for the מצוה, so they are unfit. Threads already cut to ציצית length were clearly prepared for ציצית, because nobody goes to the trouble of cutting decorative cloak threads that way. This ברייתא states outright the reasoning of step 14 ('a person does not go to the trouble'), which supports it against רבא's challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Sky-blue dye or wool used for ציצית
Strips of combed, dyed wool (not yet spun into thread)
Threads cut into short, ציצית-length pieces
Goes to the trouble, exerts himself
Go out and teach them

steps.confusionAlert: אהבה here is a person's name, the son of רבי זירא. It does not mean 'love' in this sentence.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Ahava his son:
Go out and teach them:
One who finds sky-blue dyed material in the marketplace,
if it is strips, they are unfit,
if it is cut threads, they are fit,
phrases.notes: Cut to ציצית length, which shows they were made for the מצוה

phrases.english: because a person does not go to that trouble.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא לְאַהֲבָה בְּרֵיהּ פּוֹק תְּנִי לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge in steps 15-16 by bringing a ברייתא that supports 'people do not bother'
steps.raayaObject: The principle that a person does not go to the trouble of imitating a מצוה object
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about found תכלת, taught by רבי זירא through his son אהבה

steps.title: רבא says אהבה's teaching is not decisive because of the משנה about new תפילין
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the ברייתא of אהבה does not settle the matter, since the משנה rules that new תפילין are treated differently, which suggests people do bother.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Just because אהבה son of רבי זירא taught it, should we hang decorations on it? But we learned in the משנה: When is this said? With old תפילין. But with new ones, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back. One ברייתא is not strong enough to overturn the משנה, which suggests people do make imitation תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says only old תפילין may be brought in on שבת. New ones may be amulets made to look like תפילין, which means people do bother to imitate a מצוה object. So the ברייתא of אהבה contradicts the משנה instead of proving the point.

keyTerms.meaning: He hung rings on it, meaning 'Does that make it so important or decisive?'
With old ones
With new ones
Exempt, meaning he does not have to bring them in

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא repeats the line from the משנה (old vs. new תפילין). It is not starting a new topic. רבא repeats it to show that it still conflicts with the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rava said: And because he taught it,
Ahava son of Rabbi Zeira,
has he hung rings on it?!
phrases.notes: An expression meaning: does that make it authoritative?

phrases.english: But we learned: In what case is this said?
With old ones; but with new ones, he is exempt!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִשּׁוּם דְּתָנֵי לַהּ אַהֲבָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי זֵירָא כֵּיפֵי תְּלָא לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 17's proof by restating the משנה from step 16
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The ברייתא of אהבה cannot settle the question, because it conflicts with the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה about new תפילין assumes people do bother to imitate a מצוה object, so the ברייתא is contradicted and not decisive

steps.title: רבא concludes it is a dispute among the תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רבא resolves the contradiction: whether people bother to imitate a מצוה object is a dispute between תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Whether a person goes to the trouble or does not go to the trouble is a dispute between תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא stops trying to make the two sources agree. He says they come from two תנאים who disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה about new תפילין follows the view that people do bother. The ברייתא about תכלת follows the view that people do not bother. Both are valid opinions, so neither source disproves the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, which signals a new approach
Goes to the trouble or does not go to the trouble
It is a dispute among the תנאים

steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the whole discussion. Instead of a single rule, there are two opinions, and each source follows one side.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Whether one exerts himself or does not exert himself is a dispute of tannaim.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא טָרַח וְלָא טָרַח תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the conflict between the ברייתא (step 17) and the משנה (step 18) by giving them different authors
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the conflicting sources to different תנאים (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed there was one rule, so the משנה and the ברייתא had to agree
steps.terutzMaskana: Each source follows a different תנא: one holds people bother, the other holds they do not

steps.title: The ברייתא about found תפילין begins: bring them in pair by pair
steps.stepSummary: רבא starts quoting a ברייתא to show the dispute: one who finds תפילין brings them in pair by pair, whether a man or a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: One who finds תפילין brings them in pair by pair, whether a man or a woman,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins quoting the ברייתא that will show the dispute between תנאים. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The finder wears one pair (head and arm) and brings it into town, then goes back for the next pair. This is the first part of the source. The two opposing opinions will appear later in the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: He brings them in, into town or a protected place
Pair by pair, one head תפילין and one arm תפילין at a time
Whether a man or a woman

phrases.english: As it was taught: One who finds phylacteries
brings them in pair by pair,
whether a man or a woman,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the source that proves רבא's claim in step 19 that this is a dispute between תנאים
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that 'טרח ולא טרח' is a dispute between תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about one who finds תפילין (the quote continues on the next amud)
